# 12 — PHI Readiness Checklist

**Current status: this system does not handle PHI.** All data is synthetic, generated by
`medatat-testkit`. Every protection below is implemented behind the `phi` cargo feature,
which is **off by default**.

This document exists so that turning PHI on is a checklist, not an archaeology project.

## Why this is a feature flag rather than a default

Always-on PHI hardening costs real development friction:

- A redacting `Debug` means you cannot print a value while debugging.
- Zeroizing on `Drop` obscures use-after-free bugs and slows tests.
- SQLCipher requires key management, and the key file adds a second thing to keep in step
  with the database.
- Disabled core dumps make crashes harder to diagnose.

None of that buys anything while the corpus is synthetic. Feature-gating keeps the
protections written, tested, and one flag away — rather than deleted and later
reconstructed from memory.

```toml
# crates/*/Cargo.toml
[features]
default = []
phi = ["dep:getrandom", "dep:zeroize", "rusqlite/bundled-sqlcipher"]
```

```bash
cargo build --workspace                 # development: plain SQLite, printable values
cargo build --workspace --features phi  # PHI mode: encrypted, redacted, zeroized
```

Both configurations are built in CI. A change that breaks `--features phi` fails the build,
so the PHI path cannot rot while it is switched off.

---

## What the `phi` feature turns on

| Protection | Off (now) | On |
|---|---|---|
| Local database | plain SQLite | **SQLCipher**, key from an owner-only file (mode 0600) beside the database |
| `Value` `Debug` | prints the value | **redacts**: `Text(<redacted, 14 chars>)` |
| `Value` `Drop` | ordinary drop | **zeroizes** heap payloads |
| `FormView::drop` | ordinary drop | explicitly clears every `InputState` Rope |
| Core dumps | enabled | **disabled** at startup (`setrlimit` / `SetErrorMode`) |
| Value logging | permitted at `debug` | compile error via clippy lint |
| Key file unreadable or uncreatable | n/a | in-memory database, re-sync each launch |

Everything else — the schema, the sync protocol, the API, the UI — is identical in both
modes. **PHI mode changes how data is protected, never how it is shaped.** That is what
makes the switch safe to flip late.

---

## Checklist: before any real patient data

Work top to bottom. Items 1–3 are external and have long lead times; start them early.

### Legal and platform

- [ ] **1. Enterprise BAA signed with Cloudflare.** Cloudflare enters Business Associate
      Agreements only with Enterprise-level customers. The current account
      (`doug.lance@gmail.com`, personal Workers Paid) is not eligible. Workers, D1, Durable
      Objects, R2, and KV are in-scope *products*, so no re-architecture is implied — but
      the contract must exist first.
- [ ] **2. Confirm Email Sending is covered.** Cloudflare's BAA scope list names "Email
      Security", not "Email Sending". Get coverage confirmed in writing. Magic-code emails
      carry no PHI regardless ([03-API.md](03-API.md#post-authrequest)), so this is a
      belt-and-braces item.
- [ ] **3. Data residency confirmed.** `CaseDO` objects are created with
      `jurisdiction("us")`, which pins compute and storage. Verify this matches the
      obligation you are actually under.

### Code

- [ ] 4. `cargo build --workspace --features phi` is clean on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
- [ ] 5. `cargo test --workspace --features phi` passes, including:
      `store::tests::wrong_key_fails`, `core::tests::debug_redacts`,
      `ui::tests::closing_case_clears_inputs`.
- [ ] 6. **Key storage reconsidered.** The key is a mode-0600 `medatat.key` file beside the
      database, at the user's explicit instruction not to use the OS keychain
      ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) rule 11). Record what that costs, because it is the one
      protection PHI mode is otherwise bought for: a key stored next to the ciphertext
      travels with it, so a copied database directory, a synced backup, a restored Time
      Machine snapshot, or a handed-over disk image carries both halves. It protects
      nothing at all against another process running as the same user. What it does still
      buy is a database that is unreadable if the `.db` alone is exfiltrated, and file
      permissions that keep other accounts on a shared host out. That is a fair trade for
      a synthetic corpus and not obviously one for real patient data, so decide
      deliberately: keep it, move the key to a platform credential store, or require a
      passphrase at launch. Reversing it later is cheap — one module and one call site,
      `crates/medatat-store/src/keyring.rs` — which is why it is safe to defer, and no
      excuse for forgetting.
- [ ] 7. Core dumps confirmed disabled at startup on all three platforms.
- [ ] 8. Log audit: no field value reaches a log line, panic message, or tracing span at any
      level. Grep the codebase for value interpolation, and run the app at `RUST_LOG=trace`
      against a seeded case to confirm.
- [ ] 9. Benches 1 and 2 re-run **with `--features phi`**. SQLCipher adds per-page encryption
      cost; confirm the R13/R14 gates still hold rather than assuming they do.

### Deployment

- [ ] 10. **Full-disk encryption is mandated** on every client machine. SQLCipher protects
      the database file, but the OS may still page plaintext to swap. This is the only
      complete answer, and it is a deployment policy, not a code change.
- [ ] 11. Session TTLs reviewed against the operating environment (currently 12 h absolute).
- [ ] 12. A data-retention and deletion path exists. `DELETE` of a `CaseDO` and its
      `case_index` row is straightforward; confirm it meets the obligation.
- [ ] 13. Synthetic data purged from production D1, KV, and all Durable Objects.

### Decisions to revisit at this point

Two cuts become materially more expensive once real data exists. Decide **before**, not
after:

- [ ] 14. **Audit trail.** Cut deliberately
      ([ADR-0005](adr/0005-cut-audit-versioning-rules.md)). Clinical registries and
      21 CFR Part 11 environments commonly require one. Retrofitting means touching every
      write path in both the client store and the `CaseDO`, and history would begin only on
      the day it ships. This is the single most expensive omission to reverse.
- [ ] 15. **`Value::Null` semantics.** It currently conflates "not reached yet", "chart does
      not say", and "documented as absent"
      ([10-LIMITATIONS.md](10-LIMITATIONS.md#4-valuenull-conflates-three-different-things)).
      Adding a variant is cheap while the corpus is synthetic and requires a data migration
      afterwards.

---

## Until then

- Test data comes from `medatat-testkit` and nowhere else.
- Never point a development or benchmark build at a real clinical source.
- The `phi` feature stays green in CI so that flipping it is a switch, not a project.
